sources.title: Kalpana Chawla (Q237879) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-24): English label 'Kalpana Chawla', description 'American astronaut', Korean label '칼파나 촐라', born 17 March 1962, died 1 February 2003, citizenship United States and India. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

NASA Johnson Space Center, 'Kalpana Chawla (Ph.D.), NASA Astronaut (Deceased)' biographical data sheet (May 2004, read in full): degrees from Punjab Engineering College (1982), the University of Texas (1984) and the University of Colorado (1988); research at NASA Ames on powered-lift computational fluid dynamics from 1988; vice president and research scientist at Overset Methods from 1993; selection as an astronaut candidate in December 1994; assignment as prime robotic arm operator on STS-87; later crew-systems and habitability lead; STS-87 and STS-107 flights totalling 30 days 14 hours 54 minutes; her pilot and flight-instructor ratings. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE. Official institutional biography; no trait claims, and its passage on her death is not used for any row.

NASA, 'Remembering Columbia: STS-107 crew biographies' page, Kalpana Chawla entry (read for the mission-role passage only): flight engineer and Mission Specialist 2 for STS-107, a Red Team member responsible with the commander for maneuvering Columbia in support of payload-bay experiments, and the list of experiments she worked with (including the Combustion Module with its water-mist and flame-ball experiments, protein crystal growth and biotechnology units). Official mission record; the accident material on the page was not used.

NASA Johnson Space Center, 'STS-87 Space Shuttle Mission Report' (read in the sections on mission summary, robotic arm operations and the Spartan payload): the 19 November to 5 December 1997 Columbia mission, the Spartan 201-04 deployment, a failed re-grapple attempt and the manual capture by the spacewalking crew a day later, and a statement that a formal investigation board was convened. Official mission record without individual attribution; the board's findings were not found and not read, so no row or card rests on the Spartan episode.

Overset Methods, Inc., 'Overset Grid Applications on Distributed Memory MIMD Computers', progress report for NASA Grant NCC 2-806 to NASA Ames Research Center, 30 June 1994 (NASA Technical Reports Server NASA-CR-196081; Principal Investigator Dr. Kalpana Chawla; read through its abstract, objectives and structure): a study of implementing an overset-grid implicit flow solver on 128-node and 208-node Intel parallel computers, with performance data for two composite grid configurations. Research record co-authored with Sisira Weeratunga; read at abstract and outline level, not for the numerical detail.

University of Texas at Arlington College of Engineering, 'UTA Remembers Kalpana Chawla, Columbia Crew 15 Years Later', 1 February 2018 (read in full): her UTA master's degree in 1984 and research on a cross-flow fan propulsion system, her professor Don Wilson recalling her as 'highly-motivated' with 'a burning desire to excel', Astronaut Office chief Kent Rominger saying she was admired 'for her strive for perfection', and her work at Ames and Overset Methods. Alumni-office tribute with admiring recollections; counted as retrospective praise, not as independent behavioural evidence, and the presidential memorial quotation was not used.

NASASpaceFlight.com, 'STS-107: Remembering the accomplishments of the Columbia crew', 2013 (read in full, in the flight-day account): the red and blue crew shifts of the 16-day science mission, the failure of a vacuum pump in the water-mist experiment and the ground team's fix, and the statement that Kalpana Chawla offered to give up her off-duty time on flight day 13 to carry out the repair, which in the end took five astronauts and two days. Space-press retrospective built from NASA mission reports; the entry and accident passages were not used.

NASA Image and Video Library record KSC-02pd1127 ('Official portrait of astronaut Kalpana Chawla, mission specialist', 8 March 2002), NASA media usage guidelines and the Wikimedia Commons file page 'Kalpana Chawla, NASA photo portrait in orange suit.jpg' (live check 2026-10-24) -- checked for the portrait.

analytical_rigor.rationale: [src_kc_ntrs, src_kc_nasabio | 1988-1994 | NASA research record + NASA biography] She was principal investigator on a 1994 NASA grant study of a parallel overset-grid flow solver tested on 128-node and 208-node computers, after research at Ames on powered-lift flow simulation and a doctorate in aerospace engineering. Technically demanding research is documented at first hand, but the report is joint work read here at abstract and outline level, so a modest score at low confidence. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): first-pass 62 / 0.5 lowered to 58 / 0.45 because the report was read only at abstract and outline level and is co-authored.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_kc_nsf, src_kc_nasacrew | 2003 | space-press flight-day account + NASA crew record] During the STS-107 science mission she offered to give up her off-duty time on flight day 13 to repair the water-mist combustion experiment after a vacuum-pump problem, a repair the account says took five astronauts and two days. One volunteered act in one secondary account, so a modest score at low confidence.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_kc_nasabio, src_kc_uta | 1982-1998 | NASA biography + university tribute] The NASA biography records three degrees in aerospace engineering from 1982 to 1988, research and company roles in aerodynamics, a flight-instructor certificate with airplane and glider ratings, several commercial pilot licences and aerobatic flying, and later work as lead of the Astronaut Office's crew systems and habitability section. A long record of formal skill-building is documented; the UTA tribute's praise for striving to excel is retrospective and admiring, so it adds little confidence.

portrait.source: NASA official portrait of astronaut Kalpana Chawla, mission specialist, taken 8 March 2002 at Johnson Space Center (NASA photo IDs JSC2002-E-25323 and KSC-02PD-1127). Verified on the NASA Image and Video Library record KSC-02pd1127 (description 'Official portrait of astronaut Kalpana Chawla, mission specialist', dated 2002-03-08) and on the Wikimedia Commons file page, which tags it public domain as a work solely created by NASA. NASA's media usage guidelines (nasa.gov/multimedia/guidelines) state that NASA content is generally not subject to copyright in the United States; no conflicting copyright notice was found on the NASA record. Original downloaded from NASA's image library: 2400 x 3000 pixels, SHA-1 a05f97e4dbb6fa517445cf7b9217092eeddfd349; stored file downscaled once to 960 x 1200, no crop, never upscaled. Caveat: the depicted person's likeness may carry personality rights in some uses, as the Commons page notes.

provenance.notes: PREFLIGHT: QID VERIFIED LIVE: Wikidata wbgetentities (2026-10-24) for Q237879 returned en label 'Kalpana Chawla', description 'American astronaut', ko label '칼파나 촐라', born 1962-03-17, died 2003-02-01, citizenship United States and India. SLUG/QID CHECK: no data-pipeline candidate or src file for slug kalpana-chawla or QID Q237879. REGION: north_america, chosen for career base (all her professional work from graduate study on was in the United States: UTA, Colorado, NASA Ames, Overset Methods, NASA Johnson Space Center). Repo precedents for dual-heritage people are mixed (Sundar Pichai and Satya Nadella are north_america; Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar and Har Gobind Khorana are south_asia); the career-base rule used for the first pair applies here because her US citizenship and entire astronaut career are American, with Indian birth and degree recorded in nationalityCodes. VOCABULARY: occupations astronaut, engineer; fields exploration, engineering; impact domains engineering, historical; tag explorer; archetype scientific_explorer are existing labelled ids. ZERO POLITICS: memorial speeches and any national symbolism are not scored. DECEASED SUBJECT: NO inference from the Columbia accident or her death; the STS-107 accident, the Columbia Accident Investigation Board and any cause or blame were deliberately not used; entry-day passages in sources were skipped. Excluded: marriage and family, the birth-date discrepancy in some sources, honours awarded after her death, the STS-87 Spartan satellite episode as a trait row (the mission report records a failed deployment and a formal board but the board's findings were not found, so attributing the failure to anyone would be unsupported), the student-influenced 'inspiration' narratives. PORTRAIT PREFLIGHT: NASA official portrait, found; see portrait.source. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: NASA Johnson Space Center biographical data sheet (read in full). READ (7 cited non-Wikidata sources): NASA biography, NASA STS-107 crew page (role passage), STS-87 mission report (summary and Spartan sections), NASA technical report NASA-CR-196081 (abstract and outline), UTA tribute, NASASpaceFlight retrospective, plus the NASA image record and Commons page. Not opened or blocked: the Columbia Accident Investigation Board report, the STS-87 Spartan failure board report, NASA's own oral-history interviews, books on the Columbia crew, newspaper obituaries (Tribune India item found but not opened), the nasa.gov Images page (blocked, API record used). PERSPECTIVES: official institutional record (NASA biography and crew page), technical research record (NASA technical report), mission documentation (STS-87 report), university tribute (admiring, retrospective) and space-press mission account. Independent behavioural support: the NASA technical report and the NASASpaceFlight flight-day account; the UTA tribute is admiring recollection. NO COUNTER-VOICE FOUND: no source read criticises her professional conduct, and the only adverse mission event (Spartan 2 in 1997) was not scored; the profile is therefore sparse by design, with three rows at low confidence. SELF-CALIBRATION: reviewed analytical_rigor (lowered, see row), proactive_agency (kept at 55 / 0.42: single episode but score and confidence already low) and mastery_orientation (kept at 60 / 0.42: credentials are documented first-hand by NASA; praise quotes add nothing). No rows for perfectionism, collaboration or persistence because the support is retrospective praise alone. PORTRAIT: see portrait.source.
